Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government Code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are at the Azusa City Library - 729 N. Dalton Ave., Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.azusaca.gov. Persons who wish to speak in-person during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to 7:30 P.M.; cards submitted after this time will not be accepted.
Those wishing to participate during Public Comment may do so in-person at the Azusa Auditorium, or may submit written public comments by emailing PublicComment@azusaca.gov. Emailed public comments are due by 5:30 p.m. and shall be limited to no more than 250 words. Written public comments will be provided to the City Council and will be part of the record but will not be read aloud.

CONSIDERATION OF AZUSA CHAMBER OF COMMERCE PARTNERSHIP PROPOSAL FOR FISCAL
YEAR 2025-26

Deputy City Manager, De Anda – Scaia presented the item for the Council’s consideration and direction

City Council Minutes  Page | 3
September 15, 2025
 regarding a proposal submitted by the new Azusa Chamber of Commerce for continued partnership for Fiscal
Years 2025 and 2026; explained that the partnership is established through a Memorandum of Understanding
(MOU), which outlines City expectations, the general scope of services, funding levels, and performance and
reporting mechanisms.

The Chamber of Commerce Leadership, Executive Director Bolivar, Board President Ramirez, Board Members
Ramirez, Nawaya, Taylor, and Batista, and Treasurer Gallegos, provided a brief presentation summarizing their
proposal in detail; and highlighted accomplishments from the past three months, including increased
membership, the launch of impactful programs, and strengthened partnerships.

The Council engaged in discussion regarding the Chamber’s proposed Fiscal Year 2025–2026 budget and
inquired about the organization’s governance structure, specifically how the City would have representation or a
“seat at the table” within that structure.

The Chamber responded that its current budget is limited, but it anticipates generating approximately $89,000 in
revenue by Fiscal Year 2026; stated that the matter of the City serving as a voting member on the Chamber’s
Board has not yet been discussed among the Board members.

Council discussion followed concerning the urgency of the Chamber’s funding needs and the recommendation
that an annual budget may be the most appropriate option at this time; asked about the Chamber’s annual goals,
emphasized the importance of ensuring City representation if City funds are provided, and discussed whether
that representation should be as a voting or non-voting member.

Staff requested Council direction regarding the term of representation, deliverables outside of those outlined in
the staff report, funding amount, inclusion of a self-sufficiency clause, and Chamber membership goals.

The Council reached consensus to include the discussed items in the agreement with the Azusa Chamber of
Commerce; directed staff to provide the Chamber with $45,000 in funding, including retroactive payment for
the months in which no payment was made; that City representation be incorporated into the Chamber’s
governance structure and that ribbon-cutting ceremonies be conducted for all new businesses, regardless of
Chamber membership status.

Staff was directed to incorporate these revisions into the agreement and return the item to the Council in a
future meeting.

AUTHORIZATION FOR THE PURCHASE OF MOBILE COMPUTERS, PORTABLE RADIOS AND
MAINTENANCE CONTRACTS FOR A TOTAL COST OF $354,044.29

Administrative Sergeant Beaver presented a request for approval of critical technology and equipment for the
Police Department; reported that Police staff has increased over the past eight months, resulting in an immediate
need for additional mobile computers, portable radios, software, and supporting services.

Sergeant Beaver explained that the request includes the purchase of mobile computers, new L3 Harris portable
radios, connectivity software, and essential radio upgrades; announced that the total cost for the equipment is
$331,243.29, with an additional $22,801 annually for connectivity and maintenance contracts; and noted that
funding will be provided through State Supplemental Law Enforcement Services and COPS funds, with no
impact to the City’s General Fund.

The Council inquired about the duration of the warranty for the proposed equipment purchase and the timeline
for free maintenance; requested a description of the officers’ duties to better understand the operational need for
the equipment and asked whether purchasing all items at once was necessary. Additional questions were raised
regarding the useful life of the equipment.

Staff responded that the warranty period is approximately five years and that the maintenance included ensures
proper programming and ongoing system support; explained that the equipment is necessary as officers are
currently assigned to guard the Azusa Police Jail and will begin training to become armed City Security
Officers responsible for City properties and events; noted that the useful life of the equipment ranges from five
to ten years.
